label: Vietnam industrial marketing
description: Marketing design development for an industrial facility in a Vietnamese industrial park. Same geometry contract as marketing_photoreal; the place, climate and photographic register are Vietnamese.
intent: Photograph this exact camera render as a real, recently completed industrial facility inside a Vietnamese industrial park (khu công nghiệp) in the south or north of Vietnam. It must read as an unretouched photograph taken on site for the developer's brochure, not a render: real optics, real tropical light, real construction.
allowed_changes: Develop an architect-designed, buildable industrial facade before photographing it. Respond to the actual building proportions and access: a coherent wall module, strong but restrained entrance hierarchy, deep reveals and shading where useful, a durable base and clean roof-edge resolution. Offices should read as human-scale working spaces, not an oversized glass showroom; logistics doors remain practical and accessible. Replace arbitrary procedural stripes, repeated red fins and generic feature frames with one disciplined site-specific composition. Use the client accent sparingly rather than decorating every bay. Establish this design in the Design Master and repeat it consistently, never independently redesigning each image. Resolve real metal, concrete and glass with joints, fixings, restrained weathering and realistic reflections. Keep entourage modest, correctly scaled and outside architecture and access paths; develop planting only within authored zones. Preserve measured massing, continuous roofs and functional openings. Use the construction vocabulary of Vietnamese industrial parks: pre-engineered steel sheds with profiled metal roofs and walls, painted steel structure, concrete plinth walls, grade-level steel roller shutter doors under slim steel canopies, and a two- or three-storey concrete office block with aluminium windows and simple sun shading. Signage is generic and invented, never a real company.
photography: Real drone or ground photography of a Vietnamese industrial park, as a local architectural photographer would shoot it. Humid tropical daylight: bright but slightly hazy sky, soft shadows under high sun, visible atmospheric moisture towards the horizon, natural white balance. Materials keep honest texture and ordinary cleanliness of a recently handed-over project, with light dust on concrete and slight rain staining at plinths; no showroom gloss, no oversaturated sky, no dramatic filters, no CGI sharpness. Profiled metal shows real seams, fixings and slight waviness; concrete shows joints and drainage; asphalt is dark and slightly worn.
context_direction: The surroundings are a Vietnamese industrial park: wide straight internal roads of concrete or dark asphalt with painted kerbs, street lights and overhead power lines on concrete poles; rows of tropical shade trees (sao đen, dầu, bàng, xà cừ) and palms along the roads; neighbouring factories as pre-engineered sheds in white, light grey or blue profiled metal with small white office blocks, steel gates and guard houses; low perimeter walls with steel pickets. Beyond the park the land is flat: rice fields, fish ponds, scattered village houses and tree lines under a hazy sky. Resolve every placeholder volume into such a neighbouring factory; keep the project clearly the subject. Never a North American, Australian or European suburb, no brick estates, no eucalyptus, no snow or deciduous autumn trees.
prohibited: No fantasy colour, no surreal lighting, no impossible structure, no luxury-resort architecture, no real brand names or logos, no readable text other than generic signage.
